points.description: Says a queue is a data structure (or collection/container) that stores or holds elements. Accept equivalent wording such as 'a structure for storing data items'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer says only that it is a data structure/collection, or only that it stores elements, without both ideas.

levels.says: Mentions only that a queue is a data structure/collection, or only that it stores/holds elements, but not both.

points.description: States the first-in-first-out (FIFO) principle: the first element added is the first one removed. Accept equivalent wording such as 'elements leave in the same order they arrive' or 'first come, first served'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer says a queue is ordered/linear or that elements are removed in some order, but does not convey first-in-first-out.

levels.says: Describes a queue as ordered/linear or says elements are removed in order, but does not state or imply first-in-first-out.

points.description: Names both main queue operations: enqueue and dequeue. Accept equivalent wording such as adding/inserting and removing/deleting elements.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only one of the two operations is named.

levels.says: Names only enqueue or only dequeue (or only one equivalent add/remove operation).

rubric.notes: Full marks require the answer to identify a queue as a data structure storing elements, state the FIFO principle, and name both enqueue and dequeue. Part marks are available for a partial definition, an ordered-but-not-FIFO description, or naming only one operation. No marks are earned for an answer that does not identify a queue as a data structure or give its FIFO behaviour.
